### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `51d2f77e4abc6a4c2d737a63c148533a63cb31e0` — the merge of head `9aa48a7e5a1bcd99e1d200d1ee13ef004dee6908` into base `8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 51d2f77e4abc6a4c2d737a63c148533a63cb31e0 && git checkout 51d2f77e4abc6a4c2d737a63c148533a63cb31e0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89 9aa48a7e5a1bcd99e1d200d1ee13ef004dee6908 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89 && git merge --no-ff 9aa48a7e5a1bcd99e1d200d1ee13ef004dee6908

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9aa48a7e5a1bcd99e1d200d1ee13ef004dee6908`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/public-feature-registry.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/invite-entry-toolbar.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization-invite-action.test.ts, .changeset/24016-org-invite-action.md (read for ②). The remainder of the diff (the four translation bundles and invite-user-action-copy.test.ts) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.

Inputs: card #24016 (body and all six comments, including claims 6238369945 and 6240102228 and os-dev-report 6239623631), ruling 6228318638 on #24034 (letter B′), PR #24216 body, file list and the net diff against main at the head (merge-base bb7ccde66), and the 40 check-runs on the head. Not read: the dispatch order or the dispatching seat's conclusions.

Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-17T20:14Z: 33 success, 6 skipped (paths-filtered lanes: Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke), 1 still in progress (Test Core 1/6), 0 failure. Green at read time: TypeScript Type Check (the lane that runs check:generated, check:api-surface and the spec artifact gates), Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint and Repo Gates (all nine Lint lanes, check:i18n among them), Build Core, Test Core 2 through 6, and the three card-claim guards. The in-progress shard is recorded as such; this record does not wait on it, and the landing pre-check that every check is green stays the adopting seat's to confirm once it completes.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.organization.gatedInputs` gains the string `sys_organization.actions.invite_user` (4 lines, one comment plus the row). Accept set: unchanged, judged RIGHT. `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURE_NAMES` (the key set that feeds the `requiresFeature` enum on ActionSchema and ParamSchema at action.zod.ts lines 453 and 1493) is untouched; no `*.zod.ts` file, no authorable key and no describe text changes; the spec artifact lane (TypeScript Type Check) is green on the head, which is the check:generated verdict.
2. Public surface: `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` is an exported const on the `@objectstack/spec/kernel` entry; api-surface/kernel.json records its existence only, and that snapshot is unchanged. The value's inferred const tuple gains one literal. Every consumer of the element set in the tree is a guard that reads it as data: feature-gate-guard.test.ts (both legs), public-auth-features.test.ts (grammar and XOR pins), the checklist anchor at docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json which names the `organization` member and not its rows, and plugin-auth's public-feature-registry.test.ts which reads keys and semantics only. No consumer narrows or widens behaviour on the row. Judged RIGHT: bookkeeping, not a published-surface expansion. Precedent: the third mirror (`sys_member.actions.invite_user`, #11544) landed the same one-row booking and shipped in 17.3.0 under Patch Changes in both packages with the sentence "No schema, export or authorable key changes".
3. The row is entailed by the ruling, not added beside it. Ruling item 1 fixes `requiresFeature: 'organization'`; lowerRequiresFeature turns that into `features.organization != false` in the action's `visible`; the reverse leg of feature-gate-guard.test.ts reds any `features.*` reference in a platform object's `visible` that is not booked in that flag's gatedInputs. So the ruled gate cannot land without the row. The ruling's binding line is "no new spec key" and it holds; its "no spec change" sits in the workload estimate, which the guard falsifies. Judged RIGHT, and the file-surface widening was re-declared on the card (claim 6240102228, cross-lane to domain:spec) before this review.
4. Row placement under `organization` and not `multiOrgEnabled`: RIGHT. ADR-0133 states the gate is the organization capability, never multi-org, and that member-management inputs sit under `organization` while organization lifecycle actions sit under `multiOrgEnabled`; ADR-0093 D8 item 2 records the dual-flag distinction as deliberate. The new row joins the three other `invite_user` rows in the same entry.
5. Grammar pin: the path matches the `object.actions.action` form public-auth-features.test.ts requires. The reverse-walker floor (at least 37 referenced inputs) can only rise by one. RIGHT.
6. Forward leg on the cited action: `sys_organization.invite_user` declares `requiresMembershipReach: 'invite_member'` and `requiresFeature: 'organization'`; the lowered `visible` composes the grade predicate first and the feature gate last, and invite-entry-toolbar.test.ts now pins that source byte for byte over all four mirrors, which is exactly the shape the forward leg's "equals or ends with the gate" check requires. RIGHT.
7. The action's shape against ruling item 1, read in sys-organization.object.ts at the head: `type: 'api'`, `target: '/api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member'`, `recordIdParam: 'organizationId'`, `requiresFeature: 'organization'`, `requiresMembershipReach: 'invite_member'`, `variant: 'primary'`, `order: -1`, `locations: ['record_header']`. Every key is declared on ActionSchema (objectOverride line 197, locations line 1002 with `record_header` in the enum, variant line 1311, order line 1332, requiresMembershipReach line 1503, recordIdParam line 1566). The MEMBERSHIP_REACH row for invite_member admits owner, admin and delegated_admin, matching the PR body and changeset. RIGHT, item 1 verbatim.
8. Params `email` and `role`: both required, role on `INVITATION_ROLE_OPTIONS` (exported from spec identity/invitation-role-grant.ts via the identity entry), which is sys_invitation's declared shape. Both carry `objectOverride: 'sys_invitation'` because neither is a field of sys_organization; sys_invitation declares both fields (email at its line 263, role at 275); sys_member's mirror already uses the same device for `email`; the existing resolvability pin now runs over all four mirrors. RIGHT, and the only honest way to satisfy "as sys_invitation.invite_user declares them" on an object that lacks the fields.
9. `leave_organization` keeps `variant: 'danger'` and gains `order: 1` using the existing `order` key, whose own describe text is "Promotes/demotes an action toward the record_header primary button; stable". The header set at the head is set_active_organization (order unset), invite_user (-1), leave_organization (1), change_slug (unset); a stable sort gives invite, set_active, change_slug, leave: four actions against the renderer's default inline budget of three, so leave folds. The new test pins that ordering from the declared metadata alone. RIGHT, within item 1's "falls to the overflow", declared on the card (claim 6240102228), and no new key.
10. `confirmText` on leave_organization now names the organisation's environments and members, in en and the three translated bundles: ruling item 2, with no record-scope key added. The copy is RIGHT; the bundle regeneration itself is the lane seat's remainder and check:i18n is green on the head.
11. Served metadata: the sys_organization object served over the metadata API gains one action entry. That is additive data, not a new key on a payload schema, and it is the same shape as the 17.3.0 precedent. Not a narrowing: nothing is removed; the replaced confirmText is copy. RIGHT.
12. Nothing in the diff touches a governed path (Governed Surface Queue Guard green; no `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, workflow or AGENTS.md path in the file list). The PR is Tier S by this face alone, owed by `packages/spec/src/**` non-test content.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/24016-org-invite-action.md`: `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`. The PR body and the changeset body both carry `Clause-②: no` at the start of a line, with no direction arm. Clause ② asks whether the card widens a published accept set or expands the public surface (a new key on a published payload). It does neither: no key is added to any published payload, the `requiresFeature` enum is unchanged, the spec change is one registry row that only test guards consume, and the platform-objects change is additive metadata on an existing object. It is not a narrowing either. `no` with `patch` is the shape AGENTS.md's level rule allows (`yes` would force at least minor; `no (narrowing)` would be breaking), it matches the identical-shape precedent that shipped as patch in both packages at 17.3.0, and the Check Changeset gate (the level axis of check-changeset-no-major.mjs) concluded success on the head. The changeset text is accurate on every claim I could read in the code: endpoint, organizationId, both params, the grade-capped role picker (ADR-0105 D8), the owner/admin/delegated_admin grades, order -1, leave's danger variant and order 1, the four-locale confirmText, and the spec booking. Judged RIGHT.

Clause-②: no

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report 6239623631):
1. File-surface breach, one spec registry row: ANSWERED, accepted. Gate-entailed by the ruled `requiresFeature: 'organization'` (① item 3), not a new key, re-declared on the card as cross-lane to domain:spec (claim 6240102228), and this record is the CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER review that re-claim says the row owes.
2. Third edit on sys_organization, `order: 1` on leave_organization: ANSWERED, accepted. An existing key whose describe text names this exact use; measured necessary for the ruling's "falls to the overflow"; declared on the card.
3. `objectOverride: 'sys_invitation'` on both params: ANSWERED, accepted (① item 8).
4. Hand-written translated-locale values: ANSWERED, outside the contract faces. AGENTS.md's Documentation Guardrails row permits exactly this and check:i18n is green; the lane seat's ACCEPT covers the bundles.
5. Local branch housekeeping and 6. commit trailer choice: process notes with no contract bearing; nothing to answer here.

open_questions:
1. Fold leave_organization unconditionally via `component: 'action:menu'` (B) or keep `order: 1` (A): ANSWERED A. `order` is the ruling's own vocabulary; item 5 has cloud#2910 override order and variant for its own posture; B adds a second placement lever nobody ruled for. For a plain member (no invite, header at or under three actions) leave stays an outlined danger button and is never the primary, which is what the ruling forbids. No escalation.
2. Gate the invite on `organization` while its header siblings use `multiOrgEnabled`: ANSWERED A, and not a judgment call: ADR-0133 ("the gate is the organization capability, never multi-org") and ADR-0093 D8 item 2 record the split as deliberate; in single-org mode the invite being the only header action is the open-member-management posture those records describe. No escalation.

Reviewer notes for the adopting seat (not blockers):
- ADR-0133's descriptive prose says `invite_user` "is declared on three objects" and names three copies; this PR makes four. The ADR states it records no new decision, and both of its binding statements (invitation-only adds; organization-capability gate) are honoured by the fourth mirror; both symbols it anchors in invite-entry-toolbar.test.ts (INVITE_ENDPOINT, OBJECTS_BY_NAME) survive. The count is now stale prose on a Tier H surface and is not this PR's to edit; an acceptance note or a docs-only follow-up is the right carrier.
- Test Core shard 1/6 was still in progress at read time; the queue's all-green requirement is separate from this verdict.
